definitions.gloss: to get through; to overcome; to pull through
definitions.explanation: To survive or overcome a difficult situation, crisis, or challenge. Emphasizes managing to escape or endure something tough.

examples.japanese: {危機|きき}を{切|き}り{抜|ぬ}けた。
なんとか{困難|こんなん}な{状況|じょうきょう}を{切|き}り{抜|ぬ}けることができた。
examples.english: We somehow managed to get through the difficult situation.

examples.japanese: {会社|かいしゃ}は{不景気|ふけいき}の{時期|じき}をうまく{切|き}り{抜|ぬ}けて、{今|いま}では{業績|ぎょうせき}が{回復|かいふく}している。
examples.english: The company successfully weathered the recession and its performance has now recovered.

notes:
FORMATION:
A compound verb from {切|き}る (to cut) + {抜|ぬ}ける (to pass through). The image is of cutting one's way through obstacles.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {危機|きき}を{切|き}り{抜|ぬ}ける (to get through a crisis)
- {困難|こんなん}を{切|き}り{抜|ぬ}ける (to overcome difficulty)
- {窮地|きゅうち}を{切|き}り{抜|ぬ}ける (to escape a tight spot)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {乗|の}り{越|こ}える: to overcome — emphasizes conquering rather than surviving
- {凌|しの}ぐ: to endure, to weather — focuses on endurance
